literal: Even than eating, what was eaten digesting is sweet; in love, than uniting, sulking is sweet.
translation: Digesting what one has eaten is even more pleasant than the act of eating. Likewise, in love, a feigned quarrel is sweeter than the union itself.
modern: உண்பதை விட உண்ட உணவு செரிப்பது உடலுக்கு அதிக இன்பம் தரும். அதுபோலவே, காதலில் கூடி மகிழ்வதை விட ஊடல் கொள்வது அதிக இன்பம் தருவதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet draws a striking parallel between physical digestion and romantic relationships. The poet states that the digestion of food brings more comfort and pleasure to the body than the act of eating itself. Similarly, in romantic love, the playful sulking or feigned quarrel is sweeter than the actual physical union. The comparison suggests that just as digestion prepares the body to enjoy the next meal, a lovers' quarrel renews their desire and makes their subsequent reunion much more delightful.
